note: Attacker-controlled file size is parsed from the tar header (octal size field) of the gzip-decompressed tar stream; it drives how far the archive skips ahead.
To skip the file contents, KTar seeks the KCompressionDevice forward by the attacker-controlled file size (rounded up to 512); the target decompressed position is passed to KCompressionDevice::seek.

The seek distance (bytes to skip by decompressing and discarding) is derived directly from the attacker-controlled seek target; when the tar file is larger than 3*BUFFER_SIZE this distance exceeds the dummy buffer size.
Root cause: the dummy buffer is capped at 3*BUFFER_SIZE (24576) bytes even though bytesToRead may be much larger, so the buffer is smaller than the amount requested from read().
read() is called with maxlen=bytesToRead (> 24576) while dummy only holds min(bytesToRead, 24576) bytes, so the decompressor is allowed to write far beyond the end of the dummy buffer.
readData installs dummy.data() as the zlib output buffer with avail_out = maxlen = bytesToRead (the overstated capacity), telling inflate the buffer is bytesToRead bytes long.
Sink: zlib inflate writes decompressed data into zStream.next_out (dummy.data()) up to avail_out=bytesToRead bytes, overflowing the 24576-byte dummy heap buffer (heap-buffer-overflow).
